strengths: Comprehensive 6M-scale dataset spanning multiple embodied reasoning modalities (grounding, spatial reasoning, planning, in-domain simulation data) with thoughtful construction methodology
Extensive evaluation across 12 embodied reasoning benchmarks demonstrating consistent improvements over strong baselines (Embodied-R1, RoboBrain2.0) with average score of 51.3 for 8B model
Addresses important research gap: systematic investigation of VLM-to-VLA transfer, revealing that general embodied reasoning improvements don't necessarily improve downstream robot control
Practical finding that in-domain robot-specific data is more effective for VLA fine-tuning than internet-scale pre-training provides actionable insights for practitioners
Well-structured paper with clear presentation, detailed hyperparameter specifications (Tables 4-5), and commitment to release code and data for reproducibility
weaknesses: Critical absence of real robot validation: all manipulation results are simulation-only (SimplerEnv); sim-to-real gap is well-documented and claims of 'state-of-the-art' lack real-world grounding despite embodied AI focus

Limited technical novelty: architecture built on standard InternVL3, action expert uses existing flow matching (Lipman et al. 2023); primarily an engineering/data contribution rather than methodological advance

Incomplete analysis of core finding: paper shows reasoning data doesn't improve VLA but lacks diagnostic explanation; missing key ablations (e.g., training reasoning model on in-domain data, mechanistic analysis of what transfers vs. doesn't)

Questionable data quality validation: in-domain data generated by Qwen2.5VL-7B without quality metrics; SA-1B grounding data (300k samples) synthetically generated via masks and BLIP-2 without inter-annotator agreement or human validation

Experimental design concerns: small evaluation samples for some tasks (216-825 samples, Table 6), no confidence intervals or significance testing, ablations described as 'simple,' different model sizes across comparisons (2B vs. 3B vs. 7B) complicate interpretation

Contradictory narrative: title emphasizes 'synergistic embodied reasoning' but main finding is that general reasoning data doesn't synergize well with VLA; gap between motivation and results undermines central narrative
Potential dataset contamination: training uses multiple public embodied reasoning datasets; train/test split integrity relative to benchmarks not fully validated
Limited failure analysis: no discussion of task categories where method underperforms, when reasoning data helps vs. hurts, or error patterns that could provide insights

strengths: Comprehensive Vlaser-6M dataset with 6 million samples carefully curated across diverse embodied reasoning modalities (grounding, QA, planning, spatial reasoning, simulation)
Extensive evaluation on 12 embodied reasoning benchmarks with balanced comparisons against strong closed-source and open-source baselines across multiple model scales
Important empirical finding that general embodied reasoning benchmark improvements do not reliably transfer to downstream VLA robot control performance, highlighting a critical domain gap
Strong results on WidowX robot manipulation (64.6% average success with Vlaser-QA), demonstrating practical value of in-domain data
Clear presentation with comprehensive examples and visualizations of model capabilities across QA, grounding, spatial reasoning, and planning tasks
Commitment to open-source release of code, model weights, and dataset to support reproducibility and community research
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: architecture combines existing InternVL3 backbone with standard flow matching action expert; no novel model architectures, training objectives, or algorithmic contributions

Incomplete transfer learning analysis: the central finding that in-domain data outperforms out-of-domain embodied reasoning data is intuitive and unsurprising; no mechanistic insights provided into why domain shift occurs or how to address it beyond data collection

Overclaimed SOTA results: on Google Robot tasks (Table 3), Vlaser actually underperforms InternVL3-2B on several metrics (e.g., Pick Coke Can: 85.0% vs 94.3%); task-level results are mixed, contradicting the SOTA claim

Insufficient ablation studies: missing systematic analysis of individual data component contributions (grounding vs. QA vs. planning vs. spatial), data composition sensitivity, and scaling laws; only one simple ablation performed
No real robot validation: evaluation limited to simulation (SimplerEnv) only; Figure 1's claim of 'Real2Sim Evaluation' is misleading; sim-to-real transfer gap remains unvalidated

Data quality concerns: 2M in-domain samples generated using Qwen2.5VL-7B introduces potential circular dependency; no human validation or inter-annotator agreement reported; missing metrics on generated data quality
Weak statistical rigor: small sample sizes per task (216-825 in Table 6) without confidence intervals or significance tests; no error bars on any results

The paper identifies domain shift as critical but proposes no solutions—conclusion amounts to the known result that in-domain data helps, without providing actionable techniques for domain alignment or adaptation
Main WidowX improvement driven by fine-tuning on Bridge Q&A pairs (Vlaser-QA) rather than general Vlaser pretraining, raising questions about the contribution of the 6M dataset to VLA performance

strengths: Comprehensive Vlaser-6M dataset with 6M well-curated examples across multiple embodied reasoning modalities (grounding, QA, spatial reasoning, planning, in-domain robot data)
Important empirical finding that in-domain robot-specific data is substantially more effective for downstream VLA than general internet-scale embodied reasoning data—addresses critical domain gap
Strong SOTA results across 12 diverse embodied reasoning benchmarks (51.3 avg for 8B model vs 37.0 for RoboBrain2.0-7B, +10% overall)
Extensive and fair evaluation with comprehensive baselines (closed-source: GPT-4o/Gemini; open-source across 2B-8B scales) and multiple robot platforms
Clear improvements on downstream tasks when using in-domain data (64.6% WidowX with QA data vs 41.8% baseline)
Thorough documentation of training procedures, hyperparameters, and data generation methodologies enabling reproducibility
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and sound technical approach (SFT + flow-matching)
Commitment to release code, models, and data for community benefit
weaknesses: Evaluation primarily simulation-based (SimplerEnv); lacks real-world robot validation despite claiming SOTA—critical gap for robotics paper
Core insight about in-domain data effectiveness lacks rigorous analysis: what specific factors (viewpoint, action distributions, object categories) drive performance gains remains unclear
Limited architectural novelty—mainly combines existing InternVL3 backbone with standard flow-matching; contributions are primarily dataset curation and empirical findings
Incomplete ablation studies: no systematic analysis of optimal data composition ratios, limited Google Robot ablation, hyperparameter choices (H=4, δ=10) not justified
Missing statistical rigor: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or multi-seed evaluation; inconsistent evaluation sample sizes across tasks (240-825)
Insufficient analysis of why in-domain QA data causes large jump (43.2%→64.6% on WidowX)—format, alignment, or other factors?
Dataset composition details sparse: real vs synthetic data distribution, data quality metrics, and potential evaluation-train overlap not addressed
Fairness concerns: different baselines trained on different data/backbones; some baseline results from other papers with potentially different protocols
Weaker Google Robot results (56.4% avg) compared to WidowX (64.6%)—raises questions about generalization of in-domain benefits across embodiments
No analysis of failure modes, generalization to novel objects/scenarios, or which specific conditions benefit most from in-domain data

strengths: Comprehensive evaluation across 12 embodied reasoning benchmarks and multiple robot platforms with extensive ablation studies demonstrating clear contribution of different data types
Large-scale Vlaser-6M dataset with systematic multi-modal data curation (grounding, QA, spatial reasoning, planning) that will be valuable for the community
Important empirical finding that in-domain robot-specific data is substantially more effective for VLA transfer than out-of-domain embodied reasoning benchmarks, challenging common assumptions
Strong empirical results achieving competitive/SOTA performance across multiple benchmarks (51.3% on embodied reasoning average, 65.1% on WidowX tasks)
Reproducibility commitment to release code, weights, and data; detailed hyperparameters and training protocols in appendices
weaknesses: Critical limitation: Complete absence of real robot validation. All experiments are simulation-only, which significantly undermines claims about embodied AI. SimToReal transfer remains a fundamental challenge, and sim-only results don't validate practical utility

Limited architectural and methodological novelty. The approach primarily combines existing components (InternVL3 backbone, flow matching from Black et al. 2024, standard MoE design). Main contribution is data curation and empirical evaluation rather than technical innovation

Core finding about domain gap (in-domain data > out-of-domain data) is somewhat predictable and lacks deep analysis. Paper documents the phenomenon but doesn't investigate why it occurs, provide principled mitigation strategies, or analyze which aspects of domain shift matter most

Potential circularity in in-domain data generation: 2M samples synthetically generated using Qwen2.5VL-7B with only 80% agreement with human evaluation. Risk of introducing systematic biases when training other VLMs on this data

Generalization concerns: Only tested on three robot embodiments; unclear how Vlaser transfers to robots with different morphologies or control spaces. In-domain data is specific to tested embodiments, limiting applicability
Missing critical ablations: No analysis of data scale vs. composition tradeoffs; no comparison of different action prediction methods; limited investigation of action expert architectural choices
Limited baseline scope: Concurrent methods (RoboBrain2.0, Embodied-R1) are all 2025 publications with unclear relationship to this work; performance margins sometimes modest

No failure case analysis or discussion of scenarios where Vlaser struggles; missing discussion of computational requirements; limited analysis of which reasoning capabilities are most critical for each task

strengths: Comprehensive empirical ablation study clearly demonstrating that in-domain robot data is critical for VLA transfer, providing valuable insights on domain shift
Well-curated Vlaser-6M dataset with diverse sources (1.5M grounding, 1.7M QA/spatial, 0.4M planning, 2M in-domain simulation data) and rigorous filtering (80% LLM-human agreement)
Broad evaluation across 12 embodied reasoning benchmarks and multiple robot platforms (WidowX, Google Robot, Aloha-AgileX) on two simulation systems
Clear ablation studies (Tables 2-4) isolating contributions of different data streams, providing actionable insights for embodied AI construction
Commitment to releasing code, models, and data supports reproducibility and community benefit
weaknesses: Critical gap: Evaluation only in simulation without real robot validation; severely limits claims about practical VLA applicability despite title and framing suggesting real-world deployment

Core finding contradicts main contribution: Vlaser-OOD (embodied reasoning pretraining) provides minimal VLA improvements (43.2% vs 41.8% baseline), suggesting 'synergistic embodied reasoning' claim is unsupported; all gains from in-domain data alone
Limited technical novelty: standard InternVL3 fine-tuning + flow-matching action expert (following π0), no novel architecture or reasoning mechanism; essentially a dataset and engineering paper

Confounded experimental design: cannot isolate whether embodied reasoning knowledge helps VLA when in-domain data differs fundamentally from reasoning benchmarks in both domain and data generation method

Methodological rigor issues: no error bars/confidence intervals despite small test sets (216-240 samples per task), no significance testing, potential data leakage from evaluation on same platforms used for in-domain data generation

Baseline comparisons mixed and inconsistent: primarily compares to InternVL3 base model; against Embodied-R1 and RoboBrain2.0 results are inconsistent across benchmarks; overclaimed as 10% overall improvement masks benchmark-specific variation
Unexplained domain shift mechanism: paper identifies that internet-scale data doesn't transfer to robot control but provides no deep analysis of why, limiting insights for future work
Presentation overstates contribution: 'synergistic embodied reasoning' title misleading given findings; key negative results buried; abstract suggests broader applicability than evidence supports

strengths: Comprehensive high-quality dataset (Vlaser-6M, 6M samples) with rigorous multi-stage curation pipeline spanning embodied reasoning, grounding, spatial intelligence, and planning
Strong state-of-the-art results on 12 embodied reasoning benchmarks (avg 51.3 for 8B model, +10% over competitors) demonstrating superior embodied understanding capabilities
Valuable insight that in-domain robot data substantially outperforms out-of-domain embodied reasoning benchmarks for downstream VLA policy learning, challenging field assumptions
Thorough multi-faceted evaluation including open-loop inference (12 benchmarks), closed-loop control (SimplerEnv, Google Robot, Aloha-AgileX), ablations on data types and hyperparameters
Clear presentation with well-organized dataset composition, comprehensive appendices, and commitment to reproducibility (code, weights, dataset release promised)
Systematic investigation of VLM-to-VLA transfer learning revealing actionable insights for future embodied model construction
weaknesses: Absence of real-world robot validation is a critical limitation; while SimplerEnv correlation is claimed, no quantitative evidence or actual deployment results provided, substantially limiting impact claims for 'general-purpose embodied AI'

Limited architectural and methodological novelty: standard supervised fine-tuning of InternVL3 + flow-matching from prior work (π0); 'synergistic' claim in title not operationalized through novel components

Incomplete analysis of domain shift finding: lacks investigation into which specific factors cause the gap (visual perspective vs. action distribution vs. scene diversity) and whether it can be mitigated through domain adaptation
Data quality concerns: LLM-based filtering achieves only ~80% agreement with humans; substantial synthetic data (SA-1B, 3D scenes) may not reflect true robot viewpoints
Limited scaling analysis: only 2B and 8B models evaluated; unclear how performance scales with larger models or whether 6M samples saturates before convergence
Robot manipulation performance is competitive but not dominant (WidowX 65.1% vs. π0 54.9%, Google Robot 59.0%) relative to dataset construction effort
Experimental design choices lack justification: single-frame observation for SimplerEnv is non-standard; different checkpoint iterations for different robots unexplained
Missing quantitative analyses: no data contribution curves (e.g., performance vs. samples per category), redundancy assessment across QA/spatial/grounding/planning, or saturation points
